# CARC Documentation

> User and researcher documentation for the UNM Center for Advanced Research Computing (CARC): high-performance computing clusters (Easley and Hopper), storage, Slurm scheduling, research software, tutorials, and training. The source repository is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) bundle: every page carries YAML frontmatter with type, provenance (generated/sources), and lifecycle (status/stale_after) fields.

Full corpus for ingestion: https://carc.unm.edu/docs/llms-full.txt

Every page's Markdown source (OKF frontmatter included) is served at its URL plus `index.md` — for example https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/slurm-intro/index.md. Agent guide: https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/ai-agents/

## Getting started

- [Good Neighbor Use Policy](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/good-neighbor-policy/): Acceptable-use rules that all CARC users agree to: account sharing, data restrictions, job monitoring, and security.
- [Learning Linux resources](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/learning-linux/): Curated external resources for learning the Linux command line.
- [Introduction to Linux](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/linux-intro/): A first tour of the Linux command line for new HPC users.
- [Logging in to CARC systems](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/logging-in/): Connect to CARC clusters with SSH from Linux, macOS, or Windows.
- [Getting started at CARC](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/overview/): Create a CARC account, join a project in ColdFront, and find support.
- [Password reset and one-time passwords](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/password-reset/): Reset your CARC password and manage one-time-password (OTP) settings.
- [SSH keys and client configuration](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/ssh-keys/): Generate SSH key pairs and configure your SSH client for convenient, secure logins.
- [Transferring data](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/transferring-data/): Move data to and from CARC systems with scp, rsync, sftp, and Globus.
- [X11 forwarding](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/getting-started/x11-forwarding/): Display graphical applications from CARC machines on your local screen with X11 forwarding.

## Systems & storage

- [Cluster specifications (legacy reference)](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/systems/cluster-specifications/): Historical hardware tables for CARC clusters, including retired systems such as Wheeler, Taos, Gibbs, and Xena. (deprecated; kept for history)
- [Systems overview](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/systems/overview/): Current CARC clusters (Easley and Hopper), storage tiers, and web portals such as JupyterHub, Open OnDemand, and XDMoD.
- [Storage and compute usage policies](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/systems/resource-limits/): Storage quotas, per-cluster partition and walltime limits, Slurm fairshare policy, and the job time-limit extension policy.
- [Storage permissions on BeeGFS](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/systems/storage-permissions/): Manage file and directory permissions, including ACLs, on CARC BeeGFS scratch storage.
- [Storage and backups](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/systems/storage/): CARC storage spaces (home, project, scratch), the real filesystem paths, retention windows, and what is backed up.

## Running jobs

- [Example Slurm scripts](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/example-slurm-scripts/): Ready-to-adapt sbatch scripts for serial, parallel, and GPU jobs.
- [GNU Parallel](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/gnu-parallel/): Run many small tasks efficiently inside a single Slurm job with GNU Parallel.
- [Environment modules](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/modules/): Find, load, and manage software with environment modules on CARC clusters.
- [PBS to Slurm migration](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/pbs-to-slurm/): Translate PBS/Torque commands and scripts to their Slurm equivalents.
- [Slurm accounting and fairshare](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/slurm-accounting/): How Slurm accounts, job accounting, and the fairshare system work at CARC.
- [Introduction to Slurm](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/slurm-intro/): Slurm basics on CARC clusters: partitions, interactive jobs, and your first batch script.
- [Slurm command reference](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/slurm-reference/): Common Slurm commands and sbatch directives with examples.
- [Submitting jobs](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/running-jobs/submitting-jobs/): Submit, monitor, and cancel batch and interactive jobs with Slurm.

## Interactive computing

- [JupyterHub](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/interactive/jupyterhub/): Run Jupyter notebooks on Hopper and Easley compute nodes through CARC JupyterHub.
- [Open OnDemand](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/interactive/open-ondemand/): Use CARC clusters from your browser: files, shells, job management, and interactive apps.

## Software

- [AlphaFold](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/alphafold/): Run AlphaFold protein structure prediction on CARC systems.
- [Conda channels and pip](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/conda-channels-pip/): Use conda channels (conda-forge, bioconda) and mix pip installs safely inside environments.
- [Managing conda environments](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/conda-environments/): Create, activate, export, and remove conda environments on CARC clusters.
- [Conda and Anaconda: introduction](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/conda-intro/): What conda is, how environments work, and how to use Anaconda/Miniconda on CARC systems.
- [Conda environments in JupyterHub](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/conda-jupyterhub/): Make your conda environments available as kernels in CARC JupyterHub.
- [CUDA-aware MPI](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/cuda-aware-mpi/): Pass GPU device pointers directly to MPI calls with the CUDA-aware OpenMPI/UCX stack, and fix the mixed-environment segfault.
- [Parallel Python with Dask and scikit-learn](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/dask-scikit-learn/): Scale scikit-learn workloads across cluster nodes from JupyterHub using Dask.
- [Installing deep learning packages](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/deep-learning-packages/): Install GPU-enabled deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) into conda environments. (draft)
- [Getting R software](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/getting-r/): Available R versions and how to load them with environment modules.
- [Gurobi optimizer with R](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/gurobi-r/): Use the Gurobi optimization solver from R on CARC clusters.
- [MPI parallelization from JupyterHub](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/jupyterhub-mpi/): Run MPI-parallel Python (mpi4py/ipyparallel) from CARC JupyterHub sessions.
- [MATLAB deep learning](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/matlab-deep-learning/): Train deep learning models in MATLAB using CARC GPU nodes. (draft)
- [MATLAB on GPUs](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/matlab-gpu/): Accelerate MATLAB computations with GPUs on CARC clusters. (draft)
- [Running MATLAB jobs](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/matlab-jobs/): Run MATLAB non-interactively in Slurm batch jobs on CARC clusters.
- [MATLAB Parallel Server](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/matlab-parallel-server/): Use MATLAB Parallel Server to scale parpool jobs across multiple nodes.
- [Parallel MATLAB: profile setup and batch submission](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/parallel-matlab/): Configure a cluster profile and submit parallel MATLAB jobs.
- [Parallel R with the future package](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/parallel-r-future/): Parallelize R code across cores and nodes using the future framework.
- [ParaView remote visualization](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/paraview/): Run the ParaView server on CARC compute nodes and connect from your desktop client.
- [PyTorch image classifier walkthrough](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/pytorch-classifier/): End-to-end example: train an image classifier with PyTorch on a CARC GPU node. (draft)
- [PyTorch on CARC GPUs](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/pytorch/): Install and run GPU-enabled PyTorch on CARC clusters. (draft)
- [Installing R packages](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/r-packages/): Install R packages into your user library on CARC systems.
- [R batch jobs with PBS (retired)](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/r-pbs-jobs/): Historical instructions for submitting R jobs with PBS/Torque, which CARC has replaced with Slurm. (deprecated; kept for history)
- [R on CARC systems](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/r-usage/): Load R, run scripts in batch jobs, and use R interactively on CARC clusters.
- [Singularity / Apptainer containers](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/singularity/): Build, pull, and run software containers on CARC clusters.
- [Apache Spark](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/spark/): Launch Apache Spark clusters inside Slurm allocations for large-scale data analysis.
- [Multi-GPU TensorFlow](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/tensorflow-multi-gpu/): Distribute TensorFlow training across multiple GPUs on a CARC node.
- [TensorFlow on CARC GPUs](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/software/tensorflow/): Install and run GPU-enabled TensorFlow on CARC clusters.

## Tutorials

- [Bayesian phylogenetics with BEAST](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/beast/): Run BEAST Bayesian evolutionary analyses on CARC clusters.
- [Variant calling with GATK](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/gatk/): A genomics variant-calling workflow using GATK best practices on CARC systems.
- [Metabarcoding analysis](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/metabarcoding/): Process environmental DNA metabarcoding data on CARC clusters.
- [Parallel CASA for radio astronomy](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/mpi-casa/): Run mpiCASA for parallel radio astronomy imaging on CARC clusters.
- [Coalescent simulation with msprime](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/msprime/): Simulate genealogical histories and genome sequences with msprime.
- [ORCA quantum chemistry](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/orca/): Run ORCA quantum chemistry calculations in parallel on CARC clusters. (draft)
- [Demographic inference with PSMC](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/psmc/): Infer population size history from diploid genomes using PSMC.
- [SimCov epidemiological simulation](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/simcov/): Run the SimCov agent-based model of SARS-CoV-2 infection dynamics in lung tissue.
- [RAD-seq analysis with Stacks](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/stacks/): Analyze restriction-site associated DNA sequencing (RAD-seq) data with Stacks.
- [VASP materials simulation](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/tutorials/vasp/): Set up and run VASP density-functional-theory calculations on CARC clusters.

## FAQ & troubleshooting

- [General FAQ](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/faq/general/): Quick answers about accounts, projects, cost, storage, software, and GPUs at CARC.
- [Troubleshooting](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/faq/troubleshooting/): Diagnose the most common problems: login failures, quota errors, pending or failing jobs, and module conflicts.

## Training

- [Video tutorials](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/training/videos/): Embedded CARC recordings: the QuickBytes tutorial series, CARC Annual Meeting talks, and research presentations from the UNMCARC YouTube channel.
- [Workshops and slides](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/training/workshops/): Slide decks from CARC workshops and university courses, organized by series, plus how to hear about upcoming sessions.

## Support

- [Acknowledging CARC](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/support/acknowledging-carc/): The acknowledgement statement to include in publications that used CARC resources.
- [Getting help](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/support/help/): Open a help ticket, email CARC support, or drop into office and consultation hours.

## About CARC

- [For AI agents](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/ai-agents/): How agents and harnesses should consume this documentation: llms.txt, per-page Markdown with OKF frontmatter, and trust signals.
- [Contributing to these docs](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/contributing/): How to edit pages, the OKF frontmatter contract, verifying migrated content, and building the site locally.
- [Facilities description](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/facilities/): Boilerplate facilities description for grant proposals: clusters, storage, networking, and the data center.
- [Mission and vision](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/mission/): CARC's vision and mission: leading and growing the computational research community at UNM.
- [Partner cyberinfrastructure](https://carc.unm.edu/docs/about/partners/): National and regional platforms CARC users can reach: ACCESS-CI, Jetstream2, CyVerse, and MESA.
